payload.scope: A human-made speech processing measure that quantifies the relative prominence of cepstral peaks compared to valleys in the quefrency domain.

definition.body: Cepstral-peak-to-valley-ratio is a speech analysis measure that computes the ratio of the maximum cepstral peak amplitude to the average cepstral valley amplitude within a defined quefrency range. Procedure: (1) compute the cepstrum of a speech frame, (2) identify local maxima (peaks) and local minima (valleys) in the quefrency axis, (3) calculate ratio of peak magnitude to mean valley magnitude. Parameters: quefrency range, peak detection threshold, smoothing window. Persistence: implemented in voice quality analysis tools, speaker verification pipelines, and pathological speech assessment. e.g.: Praat script for cepstral peak-to-valley ratio in dysphonia assessment; VoiceSauce cepstral peak-to-valley metric for vocal fold pathology; Kaldi voice quality plugin cepstral peak-valley ratio computation | not: cepstral-peak-prominence (measures individual peak height relative to local baseline); cepstral-energy (integrates magnitude across quefrency, not peak-valley contrast) [formal: ratio culmen-valle cepstralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.name: cepstrum-deconvolution
payload.scope: A signal processing procedure that uses cepstral analysis to separate convolved components of a signal, enabling dereverberation and echo cancellation by operating in the quefrency domain.

definition.body: Cepstrum-deconvolution is a signal processing procedure that uses cepstral analysis to separate convolved components of a signal by operating in the quefrency domain. Procedure: (1) compute the cepstrum of the observed signal via FFT, log, and IFFT, (2) apply a quefrency-domain window (lifter) to isolate the component of interest — typically a low-pass lifter to extract the slowly-varying spectral envelope or a high-pass lifter to extract the rapidly-varying residual, (3) reconstruct the separated component via exponentiation of the forward FFT of the windowed cepstrum. Parameters: lifter type and cutoff quefrency, quefrency range, signal window length. Persistence: implemented in speech processing toolkits for dereverberation and echo cancellation, documented in Oppenheim & Schafer DSP textbooks. e.g.: dereverberation of speech signals using cepstral liftering in HTK toolkit; echo cancellation in acoustic echo cancelers using cepstral domain processing; vocal-tract/excitation separation in speech analysis using low-pass/high-pass cepstral liftering | not: cepstral-homomorphic-filtering (broad filtering in cepstral domain, not targeted deconvolution); standard-deconvolution (frequency-domain inversion without cepstral transformation) [formal: deconvolutio-cepstralis | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

definition.body: Dereverberation is a signal processing technique for reducing or reversing the effects of acoustic reverberation on a recorded signal. Reverberation results from multiple reflected sound paths arriving at a microphone with different delays, smearing the direct sound and reducing intelligibility. Procedure: (1) model the reverberant signal as the convolution of the direct signal with a room impulse response plus noise, (2) estimate the room impulse response or equivalently the room acoustic characteristics (e.g., via speech presence likelihood, subspace methods, or neural models), (3) apply a deconvolution or filtering operation to recover the direct signal. Approaches include spectral subtraction in the cepstral domain (cepstral dereverberation), Wiener filtering in the time-frequency domain, and model-based methods using Hidden Markov Models or deep neural networks. Parameters: (1) the reverberant input signal, (2) the estimation method for room characteristics, (3) the dereverberation algorithm (subspace, spectral subtraction, Wiener, deep learning), (4) the target dereverberation level (mild cleanup vs. aggressive direct-path recovery). Persistence mechanism: implemented in telecommunications (hearing aids, conference systems, VoIP), speech recognition front-ends for robustness in reverberant environments, audio restoration software, and robotics/auralization systems. e.g.: Kaldi cepstral dereverberation for reverberated speech ASR; AMI meeting pipeline Wiener-filter dereverberation; DPRNN deep learning dereverberation on VoiceBank-DEMAND; HTK cepstral dereverberation in reverberant room ASR; REVERB challenge baseline reverberation-robust front-ends | not: cepstrum-deconvolution (specific quefrency-domain method); acoustic-echo-cancellation (removes feedback-loop echoes); noise-reduction (removes additive noise, not reverberation) [formal: dereverberatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]
